reference: Traditional uuencode 6-bit grouping and RFC 4648 supply independent fixed decode vectors. Python-free Bash assertions check file bytes and independent stat checks verify modes and lengths. No sharutils executable is available for direct CLI parity; malformed-input rejection is a separate documented contract.
coverage: Traditional uuencode from stdin to an embedded relative filename, decoded contents, and read-only mode behavior
Traditional uuencode from a relative input file with -o override and a two-byte final group
Base64-uuencode auto-detection and binary output containing NUL and 0xff
Padded base64 output to stdout with -o -
Preamble scanning before the begin header
exclusions: GNU error status, diagnostics, and partial-output cleanup comparisons are deferred because the GNU uudecode reference is absent.
The documented absolute /dev/stdout alias is deferred because fixtures prohibit absolute device paths; the safe -o - equivalent is covered.
No large records, long-line boundaries, multiple encoded streams, or hostile output path traversal are exercised.

cases.purpose: Decode the independently encoded bytes abc from stdin to the embedded relative filename and check that the encoded 0444 mode prevents owner writes.
cases.script:
uudecode <<'EOF'
begin 444 decoded.txt
#86)C
`
end
EOF
test -f decoded.txt
decoded=$(<decoded.txt)
test "$decoded" = abc
printf '%s\n' "$decoded"
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a %s" decoded.txt

cases.purpose: Read a relative encoded input file, override the embedded output name with -o, and decode the independently encoded bytes ab from a two-byte final group.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'begin 600 embedded.dat' '"86(`' '`' 'end' > input.uue
uudecode -o actual.dat input.uue
test -f actual.dat
test ! -e embedded.dat
decoded=$(<actual.dat)
test "$decoded" = ab
printf '%s\n' "$decoded"
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a %s" actual.dat

cases.purpose: Auto-detect a begin-base64 stream and emit the RFC 4648-decoded bytes 00 ff 41 to stdout without creating the embedded filename.
cases.script:
uudecode -o - <<'EOF'
begin-base64 600 ignored.dat
AP9B
====
EOF
test ! -e ignored.dat

cases.purpose: Decode the independently known padded base64 value QQ== to stdout using the safe -o - form.
cases.script:
uudecode -o - <<'EOF'
begin-base64 600 ignored.dat
QQ==
====
EOF
test ! -e ignored.dat

cases.purpose: Find a traditional begin header after ordinary preamble lines and verify the decoded relative file contents.
cases.script:
uudecode <<'EOF'
Mail subject text
An introductory line
begin 444 after-preamble.txt
#86)C
`
end
EOF
test -f after-preamble.txt
decoded=$(<after-preamble.txt)
test "$decoded" = abc
printf '%s\n' "$decoded"
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a %s" after-preamble.txt

cases.purpose: Create an empty relative output file from the traditional zero-length record and honor its read-only mode behavior.
cases.script:
uudecode <<'EOF'
begin 444 empty.dat
`
end
EOF
test -f empty.dat
test ! -s empty.dat
printf '%s\n' 'empty file verified'
/usr/bin/stat -c "%a %s" empty.dat

cases.purpose: Check the documented -m no-op option while decoding the independently encoded traditional payload abc to stdout.
Check the Bash builtin type and that its registered help topic is available; this is metadata coverage, not decoder operation coverage.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t uudecode)
[[ $kind == builtin ]]
help uudecode > metadata.out
printf '%s\n' "$kind"

cases.purpose: Compare the full GNU malformed-input status, diagnostic and partial-output cleanup behavior beyond the independently checked rejection contracts.
cases.reason: The semantic rejection contracts executed. GNU byte/status parity needs sharutils added to the image, which is root's image change.

cases.purpose: The source documents an absolute /dev/stdout output alias in addition to -o -.
Reject input containing no begin header with failure and a diagnostic.
Reject an invalid base64 alphabet and remove the incomplete output file, preserving the diagnostic.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'begin-base64 600 decoded' '!!!!' '====' > input
if uudecode input; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ ! -e decoded ]] || exit 90
exit "$rc"
